subject: Problems estimating global abundance in R

messages.author: df51387064954b5e
messages.subject: Problems estimating global abundance in R
parts:
Dear all,

I am using the package “dsm” in R to make density surface modeling of data collected from systematic line-transect surveys of 9 different years, for the same study area. For the DSM the detection function and cluster size have been fitted over all years. The question is:

How can I estimate global abundance for the whole data set, taking into account the annual variation in the environmental variables?

The package I am using now, estimates the MEAN abundance over these 9 years, calculating the mean abundance for each cell of the prediction grid with the model predictions of the 9 years separately.

I think that this is not a good way to predict global abundance over all years, because it does not take into account the spacial and temporal component of my data. So, does anyone knows how can I estimate the global abundance, avoiding use the mean of the annual predictions? Statistically, what is the best and right way to estimate it?

Thank you,
Paula.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Problems estimating global abundance in R
parts:
Complicated question, with many possible answers.

Do you believe the detection function changes each year, do you believe the cluster size dynamics changes each year; do you believe the relationship of animal location and environmental covariates change each year?  If yes, then the flippant answer is to fit separate detection functions and spatial models to each years' data.  That approach is not commonly taken.

At the other extreme, if you believe the detection function, cluster size dynamics and covariate response does not change over the study, then fit a single detection and dsm model.  Build separate prediction grids using the annual values for the environmental covariates, produce annual predictions from the prediction grids, acknowledge the variation in the annual estimates. 

There are many more variants of those approaches that could be taken.  Others will doubtless offer you other suggestions.
